newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Hanson calls active amid bid talk.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Hanson calls active amid bid talk.

text.p: Call options on Hanson Plc, in the throes of a demerger, were active amid vague rumours that Hanson itself may be the subject of a impending bid, dealers said.
A UK major bank bought 2,000 February 119 calls at 7-1/2p, which helped boost the underlying shares, they said.
Hanson stock, up 1/2p to 81p at 1201 GMT on heavy volume of 8.6 million shares, would only have to rise a few pence from their current level for the trade to be profitable, dealers said.
That's because Hanson calls entitle the holder to buy 1/10 of a share of Imperial Tobacco, one of Hanson's demerged units, for every full share of Hanson.
Dealers said bid speculation crept into the market yesterday, buoying Hanson shares and trading volume.
"I think you have to give it some credibility because the share price is so cheap," said one marketmaker.
The stock fell sharply after the details of its demerger were announced.

Elsewhere, dealers noted the purchase of 4,000 January 650 calls on British Petroleum. The buyer paid 48p for the calls, and was thought to have purchased the calls against the stock as a volatility trade.
British Petroleum shares were down 1-1/2p at 686-1/2 on heavy volume of more than 10 million shares.
